heading.en: Too much demand, or too little?
heading.kn: ಬೇಡಿಕೆ ಅತಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚೇ ಅಥವಾ ಅತಿ ಕಡಿಮೆಯೇ?

hook.en: In a festival season, shops run out of stock and prices jump. In a slowdown, factories cut shifts and workers lose jobs. Both come from aggregate demand not matching what the economy can produce at *full employment*. How can the government and the RBI fix each problem?
hook.kn: ಹಬ್ಬದ ಕಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಂಗಡಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸರಕು ಖಾಲಿಯಾಗಿ ಬೆಲೆಗಳು ಏರುತ್ತವೆ. ಹಿಂಜರಿತದಲ್ಲಿ ಕಾರ್ಖಾನೆಗಳು ಪಾಳಿ ಕಡಿತಗೊಳಿಸಿ ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕರು ಕೆಲಸ ಕಳೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಎರಡಕ್ಕೂ ಕಾರಣ ಸಮಗ್ರ ಬೇಡಿಕೆ ಪೂರ್ಣ ಉದ್ಯೋಗ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆಗೆ ಹೊಂದದಿರುವುದು. ಸರ್ಕಾರ ಮತ್ತು RBI ಇವನ್ನು ಹೇಗೆ ಸರಿಪಡಿಸುತ್ತವೆ?

title.en: Define full employment and involuntary unemployment
Explain excess demand (inflationary gap) and deficient demand (deflationary gap)
List fiscal and monetary measures to correct them

say.en: In a festival season, shops run out of stock and prices jump. In a slowdown, factories cut shifts and workers lose jobs. Both come from aggregate demand not matching what the economy can produce at full employment. How can the government and the RBI fix each problem? In this lesson: Define full employment and involuntary unemployment.
Explain excess demand inflationary gap and deficient demand deflationary gap.
List fiscal and monetary measures to correct them.

body.en: *Full employment* is a situation in which everyone who is able and willing to work at the prevailing wage rate gets work. Even then some people may be voluntarily unemployed (unwilling to work at that wage) or between jobs. Involuntary unemployment exists when people are willing to work at the prevailing wage but cannot find work. Keynes showed that equilibrium income can settle below the full employment level.

points.en: *Full employment*: all willing workers at the current wage are employed
Voluntary unemployment can exist at *full employment*

narration.kn: ಪೂರ್ಣ ಉದ್ಯೋಗ ಎಂದರೆ ಪ್ರಚಲಿತ ಕೂಲಿ ದರದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡಲು ಸಮರ್ಥರೂ ಇಚ್ಛಿಸುವವರೂ ಆದ ಎಲ್ಲರಿಗೂ ಕೆಲಸ ಸಿಗುವ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ. ಪ್ರಚಲಿತ ಕೂಲಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡಲು ಸಿದ್ಧರಿದ್ದರೂ ಕೆಲಸ ಸಿಗದಿದ್ದರೆ ಅದು ಅನೈಚ್ಛಿಕ ನಿರುದ್ಯೋಗ. ಸಮತೋಲನ ಆದಾಯ ಪೂರ್ಣ ಉದ್ಯೋಗಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಕೆಳಗೆ ನಿಲ್ಲಬಹುದು ಎಂದು ಕೇನ್ಸ್ ತೋರಿಸಿದರು.

title.en: On the board: Inflationary and deflationary gaps

narration.en: The gap between aggregate demand and full employment output decides whether we face inflation or unemployment.

say.en: Full employment output is 800. The 45 degree line shows output.
If AD is 260 plus 0.75 Y, then at 800 demand is 860: sixty more than output. That is excess demand.
If AD is 120 plus 0.75 Y, demand at 800 is only 720: eighty short. That is deficient demand.
Excess demand raises prices, not output. Deficient demand lowers output and jobs.
The cures are opposite. Fiscal tools are spending and taxes; monetary tools are the RBI’s rates and operations.
The gap between aggregate demand and full employment output decides whether we face inflation or unemployment.

body.en: Excess demand: aggregate demand is more than output at full employment. The excess is the inflationary gap. Output cannot rise, so prices rise. *Deficient demand*: aggregate demand is less than output at full employment. The shortfall is the deflationary gap. Output and employment fall, causing involuntary unemployment. Fiscal policy (government spending and taxes) and monetary policy (repo rate, bank rate, CRR, SLR, open market operations, margin requirements) can close either gap.

points.en: Inflationary gap = AD at Yf − Yf
Deflationary gap = Yf − AD at Yf
Monetary tools: repo rate, CRR, SLR, OMO, margins

problem.en: Full employment output is ₹800 crore. C = 60 + 0.75Y and I = ₹200 crore. (a) Find AD at full employment and name the gap. (b) By how much must autonomous spending change to close it?

steps.en: AD exceeds output by 860 − 800 = ₹60 crore: an inflationary gap (excess demand).
(b) Cut autonomous spending (for example government spending or investment) by ₹60 crore, so that AD at 800 = 800.
Check: new Ā = 200, Y* = 200/(1 − 0.75) = ₹800 crore = full employment output.

answer.en: (a) AD = ₹860 crore; inflationary gap of ₹60 crore. (b) Reduce autonomous spending by ₹60 crore.
